summary: The solver-visible continuity contract is explicit, naturally delegated from instruction.md, and almost all substantive verifier behavior maps cleanly to it. However, two material contract clauses are not meaningfully discriminated by the current verifier: convergence never tests the confirmed generation last_observed_sequence watermark against a competing journal/archive extent, and recovery fencing never tests a token becoming stale in the boundary after one replay item has completed but before the next item is published. Plausible implementations that use the wrong convergence authority or omit the between-items fence check can satisfy the current suite. Under the Q4 contract, these material coverage gaps require REVISE.

evidence.observation: Q4 requires independent bidirectional requirement/test mapping and mandates REVISE for any material phantom test, untested requirement, or grading-relevant ambiguity.

The handoff identifies the incident, immutable captured history, operator entrypoints, output paths, and explicitly delegates durability/replay semantics to /app/continuity/docs/ without enumerating hidden tests.

The delegated contract explicitly defines stable event identity, physical-stream acknowledgement, generation authority, source topology, crash-safe consumer effects, quarantine, reconciliation by origin identity, confirmed-watermark convergence, replay, fencing, retention, diagnostics, and report truth.

The core behavioral suite exercises stable retry identity, wrong-stream publish acknowledgements, generation holds, source/domain and checksum mismatches, effect/checkpoint crash boundaries, quarantine, hub-sequence independence, missing identities, replay planning, retention, and fencing.

The contract-coverage suite invokes the real operator CLI, independently derives report truth from configuration and SQLite state, protects captured incident evidence, checks diagnostic non-mutation, and exercises real NATS replay plus generation/lease/retention entrypoints.

Both confirmed generations have last_observed_sequence=6000 and each region's journal contains origin sequences 1..6000, so the current convergence scenarios do not distinguish the confirmed generation watermark from journal extent.
continuityctl execute-replay constructs a NatsPublisher and passes it to engine.execute_replay_plan; verify calls the real engine health/reconciliation paths and writes the declared reports.

The starter contains genuine broken implementations for the F2P surfaces, including retry-specific message IDs, premature publication state, aggregate-hub reconciliation, count-derived replay, unsafe retention, and incomplete fencing, so the reviewed F2P tests reach real starter defects rather than manufactured no-op failures.

findings.criterion: Every material solver-visible requirement has meaningful behavioral coverage; confirmed convergence must use the generation registry last_observed_sequence as the authoritative watermark.
findings.why_it_matters: The contract says convergence is measured against the confirmed generation registry watermark, not merely the maximum journal sequence or another coincident extent. Every current convergence fixture keeps last_observed_sequence equal to the journal high-water mark (6000). A plausible repair that derives its target from journal extent instead of the confirmed generation watermark therefore passes these tests while violating the stated authority rule.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add one behavioral scenario in which the confirmed generation last_observed_sequence intentionally differs from a competing journal/archive extent, then assert archive completeness, required-consumer lag, and CONVERGED/DIVERGED status against the confirmed watermark. Keep the requirement wording unchanged.
findings.regression_risk: Low if added as an isolated cloned-state verifier scenario; it should not require changing solver-visible prose or existing production interfaces.

findings.criterion: Every material solver-visible requirement has meaningful behavioral coverage; replay fencing must be enforced at entry, between replay items, and after an in-flight publish returns before replay-state mutation.
findings.why_it_matters: The existing stale-worker test independently covers a stale token at entry and a lease rotation during the first publish, which verifies the post-publish recheck before replay-item mutation. It never completes one replay item under a valid token and then makes that token stale before the next item begins. An implementation that checks only at entry and after publishes, but omits the pre-item/between-items check, can pass the current test while issuing one unauthorized next-item publication after ownership changed.
findings.minimal_remediation: Add a two-item replay scenario that lets item one complete, rotates or expires the lease before item two starts, and asserts item two is not published and no stale replay-state mutation occurs. Preserve the existing entry and in-flight-post-publish cases.
findings.regression_risk: Low to medium; the scenario must control the boundary deterministically without introducing timing flakiness.

change_scope: Verifier coverage only: add a confirmed-watermark discriminator scenario.
Verifier coverage only: add a deterministic between-replay-items fencing scenario.
do_not_change: task runtime/solution solely to satisfy this review

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.requirement: Stable event_id is the publish/replay idempotency authority and distinct stable identities remain distinct even for equal payloads.
Journal publication succeeds only after a positive acknowledgement for the expected physical origin stream; failures/wrong-stream acknowledgements remain retryable.
Origin generations are explicit; ambiguous resets remain pending until approval, matching generations advance monotonically, and historical events retain their accepted generation.
The hub raw archive is source-only and does not admit local raw telemetry writes.
Physical stream names and region source-domain ownership are unambiguous and correctly configured.
Archive reconciliation preserves and validates stable origin identity metadata, source ownership, and payload checksum without using invalid event identities.
Redelivery of one stable event cannot create a duplicate committed downstream business effect.
Effect commit precedes application progress/acknowledgement advancement, crash-after-effect-before-ack is idempotent, and failed effect commits advance neither effect nor acknowledgement progress.
Poison input creates durable quarantine evidence without a committed business dispatch or completed application/ack progress.
Restart/consumer health compares JetStream acknowledgement evidence with durable application effect/checkpoint state instead of trusting broker progress alone.
Reconciliation is keyed by stable event/origin identity; hub aggregate positions cannot substitute for origin completeness, and reported contiguous archive progress is origin-sequence based.
Missing and unexpected stable identities are detected even when aggregate counts offset.
Convergence uses the confirmed generation last_observed_sequence watermark and requires both contiguous archive-origin progress and every enabled required consumer application progress to reach it.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.gap: Current fixtures make confirmed last_observed_sequence equal the journal high-water mark, so they do not discriminate the required watermark authority.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.requirement: Replay planning contains only genuinely missing stable identities for one approved generation and blocks unapproved generation recovery.
Durable archive/effect identity remains authoritative after server duplicate-window expiry.
Cleanup does not cross contiguous archive-origin progress and fully converged old rows can become eligible.
Cleanup does not cross the slowest enabled required consumer application checkpoint.
Approved/running replay plans pin referenced journal authority, while terminal plans release that retention pin.
Configured edge and hub raw retention cover maximum disconnect plus replay plus safety margin.

Recovery leases use monotonically fenced epochs; stale tokens are rejected at replay entry, between items, and after in-flight publish before replay-state mutation; stale renew/release cannot mutate the current lease.
REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.gap: Entry and post-publish fencing are discriminated, but no scenario makes the token stale after one item completes and before the next item begins.

REQUIREMENT_TEST_MATRIX.requirement: Active replay ranges for the same region/generation cannot overlap, while disjoint active ranges may coexist.
Derived consumer output remains outside the raw sourced telemetry namespace.
Cleanup excludes rows younger than minimum journal age and rows with explicit retention holds.
Real verify materializes health.json and reconciliation.json from durable truth without rewriting captured incident evidence, and health dimensions are independently checkable.
inspect, reconcile, and verify remain diagnostic with respect to recovery/business state while permitting diagnostic reconciliation records/findings.
Non-diagnostic generation, replay, lease, execution, and retention operator entrypoints remain wired to durable production behavior, including the real NatsPublisher/JetStream replay path.

UNTESTED_REQUIREMENTS.missing_behavior: A scenario that makes the confirmed generation last_observed_sequence differ from a competing journal/archive extent so the verifier proves the confirmed watermark is the convergence authority.
A scenario that makes a valid replay token stale after one item completes and before the next item begins, proving the next publish is fenced before it occurs.

DELEGATED_CONTRACT_CHECK.observation: instruction.md explicitly points solvers to /app/continuity/docs/ for durability and replay rules; continuity-contract.md exists there and states the graded invariants at operational/behavioral level.
